items.t: Children and adolescents with open growth plates → Fracture (paeds) set
Primary survey / resuscitation of major trauma → resuscitation card first (PHC STG 21.3.7)
Head injury → TBI pathway · spinal cord injury → own pathway
Facial, skull and isolated rib/chest injuries → own pathways

admission.title: Diagnostic criteria — any one confirms fracture

items.t: X-ray: fracture on 2 views (AP + lateral), joint above and below
Clinical deformity, crepitus or abnormal movement (X-ray to classify)
High suspicion, X-ray normal → treat as fracture and re-image
Snuffbox tenderness: thumb spica, repeat X-ray at 14–21 d
Hip pain, cannot bear weight after fall: REFER for CT/MRI
X-ray if Ottawa ankle/foot/knee rule positive
Site ____ Side L / R · Time of injury ____ · Energy: low / high
Open fracture (any wound over or near the fracture)
Neurovascular deficit distal to the fracture
Hip, femoral shaft, pelvic ring or spinal fracture
Major mechanism or more than one body region injured
Neck, chest, abdominal or pelvic pain
Assault, intimate partner or elder abuse

admission.note: Abnormal = outside norms or the patient's documented baseline

items.t: Pain on passive stretch of digits

Still pulseless or white after realignment: EMERGENCY REFER
Passive-stretch pain / tense compartment: split cast and padding to skin, limb at heart level, EMERGENCY REFER

admission.title: Red flags to rule out on arrival

decision.t: 10. Diagnosis = COMPLICATED or OPERATIVE FRACTURE → splint, analgesia, antibiotics if open, then REFER
11. ADMIT — or cast and discharge if §2 and §9 are clear; continue on the Fracture inpatient chart and the 24-hour neurovascular record

manage.t: Broad arm sling 2–4 wk, then ROM; no reduction

refer.t: Open / skin tenting · NV deficit · shortening > 2 cm · > 100% displaced (active) · floating shoulder

manage.t: Sling/collar & cuff 2–3 wk, early pendulum ROM

refer.t: Greater tuberosity > 5 mm · displaced 3–4 part · head-split · fracture-dislocation (urgent)

confirm.t: AP + lateral incl. shoulder and elbow

manage.t: U-slab (coaptation) 7–10 d → functional brace to union; arm hangs free

refer.t: Open · NV compromise · floating elbow · pathological · ant. angle > 20°, varus > 30°, short > 3 cm · radial palsy alone = observe

manage.t: Above-elbow backslab at 90°, elevate

refer.t: ALL displaced → REFER (ORIF)

manage.t: Undisplaced, extension intact: above-elbow backslab
45–90° for 3 wk

manage.t: Mason I: sling 3–7 d, early ROM

refer.t: Block to rotation · > 2 mm displaced · Mason III/IV · elbow instability

features.t: Check radiocapitellar line and DRUJ on every forearm film

confirm.t: AP + lateral forearm incl. elbow and wrist

manage.t: Above-elbow backslab at 90°, elevate until transfer

refer.t: ALL adult both-bone, Monteggia, Galeazzi → REFER (ORIF)

About 6 wk

refer.t: Outside those limits · proximal third (Monteggia)

features.t: Fall on outstretched hand; check median nerve

manage.t: Extra-articular, stable: reduce (haematoma block) + below-elbow backslab → cast; avoid extreme flexion/ulnar deviation
About 6 wk

manage.t: Undisplaced: thumb spica (below-elbow) cast
6–12 wk by site
Suspected, X-ray normal: spica, repeat X-ray at 14–21 d

Accept neck angle: index/long 10–15°, ring 30–40°, little 50–70°

1st MC base (Bennett)

manage.t: Analgesia, deep breathing; admit elderly or ≥ 3 ribs

manage.t: Neuro intact, stable wedge: mobilise as tolerated ± brace
Cervical: collar, REFER all

VTE prophylaxis (box, side 2)
Unstable: binder over greater trochanters

NWB; X-ray weekly first 3 wk

refer.t: ALL → REFER

Displaced talar neck (urgent)

chart.phase_note: Branch rows A–D: complete only the branch that applies

standing.t: Neurovascular check hourly for 24 h after injury, reduction or new cast, then 4-hourly while admitted if all normal
Colour & warmth, capillary refill, pulse, sensation, movement — compare with the other limb
Pain score with every check; pain on passive stretch of fingers/toes = call doctor
Elevate the limb; keep at heart level if compartment syndrome is suspected
Cast/splint check: tight, wet, cracked, rubbing; wound ooze
After IV morphine: obs every 5 min for at least 20 min after the last bolus
Pulse, BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature 4-hourly on the observation chart; pressure care if immobile

rows.label: 0 h
rows.lead: Primary survey first. Check the referral note for analgesia, antibiotic and tetanus already given — do not duplicate.

feed.t: Elevate; heart level if compartment concern
Nil by mouth if reduction or transfer likely
2 large-bore IV lines if open, femur, pelvis or shock

tests.t: X-ray per §8 (AP + lateral, joint above and below)
Hb if femur, pelvis, open or multiple fractures
HGT + ECG if older fall or collapse

treatment.t: Control bleeding: pressure; tourniquet max 6 h
NaCl 0.9% IV; > 1 L needed → blood; keep total crystalloid < 1.5 L
O-neg emergency blood (2 units on site) + lyophilised plasma 1 unit per unit of blood → REFER
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h — only if < 3 h from injury
Pelvis + shock: binder over greater trochanters
Remove gross debris, saline-soaked dressing, splint; antibiotic within 1 h (side 2)
Tetanus toxoid 0.5 mL IM if no dose in 5 years
Morphine IV 3–5 mg, titrate, total max 10 mg (side 2)
Realign or reduce under analgesia/sedation, splint, recheck in 15 min

tests.t: X-ray reviewed — tick the working diagnosis (Doc 1 p2–3)

treatment.t: Decide: cast at ANDH / REFER (operative criteria) / admit for observation

feed.t: Sterile saline dressing, backslab; do not irrigate in casualty

treatment.t: Cefazolin IV by weight (side 2); Gustilo III add gentamicin
REFER for debridement: within 24 h (III), 12 h (IIIB tibia), 6–12 h gross contamination

feed.t: Split cast and padding to skin; limb at heart level

tests.t: NV check every 15 min until resolved or transferred

treatment.t: Compartment syndrome → EMERGENCY REFER for fasciotomy

feed.t: Skin traction / Thomas splint; pelvic binder if unstable

treatment.t: REFER: hip within 24–48 h; femoral shaft nail within 24 h

feed.t: Reduce under haematoma block or procedural sedation
Backslab (not full cast) for the first 24–48 h while swelling settles

tests.t: NV → 4-hourly if all normal for 24 h
Check X-ray if manipulated or cast changed

treatment.t: Oral analgesia; constipation prevention on opioids
Watch for fat embolism, VTE, delirium, pressure sores

items.t: Paracetamol 500 mg–1 g PO 4–6-hourly, max 4 g/24 h (15 mg/kg/dose)
+ Ibuprofen 400 mg PO 8-hourly with meals — not if hypovolaemic, renal impairment, GI bleed or pregnant
+ Tramadol 50–100 mg PO 6-hourly, max 400 mg/d; avoid head injury, epilepsy
Morphine IV 3–5 mg, titrate, total max 10 mg; or IM 0.1–0.2 mg/kg 4-hourly
Nil by mouth: diclofenac 75 mg deep IM 12-hourly, max 2 days
Lidocaine (haematoma or fascia iliaca block): max 3 mg/kg
Reduction under procedural sedation per ANDH sedation/RSI card
Cefazolin IV 8-hourly: < 60 kg 1 g · 60–120 kg 2 g · ≥ 120 kg 3 g
Gustilo III: add gentamicin 6 mg/kg IV daily
Continue 24 h after wound closure (48 h for type III if closure delayed)
Toxoid 0.5 mL IM if no dose in the last 5 years
Never immunised + dirty wound: add tetanus immunoglobulin
Pelvis/acetabulum, non-operative: aspirin 150 mg daily (low–moderate risk) or enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily (high risk), up to 35 d
Lower-limb cast + immobile: assess VTE risk
Pain out of proportion; pain on passive stretch (earliest); paraesthesia; tense compartment; pulse often present until late
Split cast to skin, heart level, EMERGENCY REFER
Tight, wet, cracked, rubbing, smell → split/replace
Drowsy, slow breathing → stop opioid, naloxone, call doctor

discharge.title: Discharge / transfer criteria — all must be met

items.t: NV normal at last check, ≥ 2 h after reduction/cast
Safe with crutches / sling; weight-bearing explained
Follow-up or transfer booked; abuse concern addressed
Cast/X-ray check at 1 week (2 weeks if reduced/unstable); cast off per sheet; physio
Pain getting worse despite tablets · numb or tingling · fingers/toes pale, blue or cold · cannot move fingers/toes · cast tight, cracked, wet, smelly or loose · fever · calf pain or breathlessness
Keep raised above heart for 48 h, move free joints, keep cast dry, nothing inside the cast

nursing.title: 24-hour neurovascular record — pain, circulation, sensation, movement
nursing.period: One sheet per 24 h; hourly rows, heavier rule every 4 h

items.t: Neurovascular check hourly for 24 h after injury, reduction or new cast, then 4-hourly while admitted if all normal
Colour & warmth, capillary refill, pulse, sensation, movement — compare with the other limb
Pain score with every check; pain on passive stretch of fingers/toes = call doctor
Pain not settling with prescribed analgesia = call doctor
After IV morphine: obs every 5 min for at least 20 min after the last bolus
Elevate; heart level if compartment concern
Cast tight, wet, cracked, rubbing; wound ooze

call.t: Call the doctor for: pain increasing or out of proportion, pain on passive stretch, new numbness or tingling, pale/dusky/cold limb or slower capillary refill than the other side, absent pulse, unable to move fingers/toes, cast tight/wet/cracked, drowsy or slow breathing after opioid, new confusion or falling SpO₂
